title: China proposes tighter algorithm rules, broader protections for platform workers
key_facts: Seven central departments, including the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security, released a draft on Thursday 8 Oct 2026; comments open until 8 Nov.
It covers internet-based workers such as ride-hailing drivers, food delivery workers and livestreamers.
Wages must be paid in full and on time in cash; higher pay for official public holidays; rest after four hours of continuous work.
Employers must respond to objections within 48 hours.
Algorithm use must not discriminate in order allocation and pay.
Per Free Malaysia Today: platforms must sign employment agreements, explain management algorithms; stopping orders or banning accounts cannot be decided by algorithm alone.
China had 280 million flexible workers in 2025, per a think tank cited by Free Malaysia Today.
quote_evidence: China has released draft measures to strengthen the protection of working rights for people in new forms of employment, including ride-hailing drivers, food delivery workers and livestreamers.

Platforms must also explain their management algorithms to workers, according to the proposal, and decisions to stop orders or ban worker accounts cannot be made by algorithm alone and must be reviewed manually.
why_it_matters_hint: China is extending labour protections and algorithm limits to platform workers.
notes: MLex page paywalled. Read at China Daily (state-run outlet, so the framing is the official one; its text describes the draft) and Free Malaysia Today (EPA photo, likely a wire story; wire not named, so not credited). MLex headline also mentions tighter algorithm rules.
